Consult Summary:
40-year-old woman with childhood asthma presents with 2-day history of worsening wheeze and exertional shortness of breath after heavy dust exposure while cleaning. Virtual review—no vitals available—plan is urgent in-person GP visit for pulse oximetry, possible steroids, and OTC/ prescribed antihistamine.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute wheeze / shortness of breath (possible asthma exacerbation vs dust-induced allergic reaction)
- Onset: ~1 hour after cleaning dusty carpet 2 days ago; progressive, worse at night.
- Symptoms: Wheeze, short of breath, difficulty finishing sentences; no chest pain, no dizziness.
- Pertinent negatives: No chest pain on deep breath; no dizziness/vertigo.
- Relevant history: Childhood asthma; occasional exercise-induced symptoms; hay fever.
- Medications taken for episode: none; still has an old asthma inhaler but has not used it.
- Planned assessment: In-person GP review for pulse oximetry and further evaluation; consider need for oral steroids.

Issue 2: History of asthma
- Childhood asthma, occasionally symptomatic with prolonged running; possesses inhaler (type/dose/frequency not documented); not under regular GP review.
- Previous use of oral steroids for asthma (dates/doses not documented).

Issue 3: Seasonal allergic rhinitis (hay fever)
- Occurs in summer; usually unmanaged (no regular antihistamine).
- Current episode may be dust-triggered; advised trial of OTC antihistamine.

Medications:
- Asthma inhaler (specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented; patient last used “a couple of months ago”).
- Past course(s) of oral steroids for asthma (details not documented).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Childhood asthma (intermittent adult symptoms).
- Hay fever / allergic rhinitis.

Social History:
- Not discussed (smoking status, alcohol, occupation, living arrangements not documented).

Preventative History:
- None discussed (cervical screening, vaccinations, etc. not documented).

Physical Examination:
- No in-consult examination performed; no vitals recorded (virtual consultation).

Plan:
- Attend local GP surgery today/ASAP for:
  • Pulse oximetry and clinical assessment.
  • Consider spirometry/peak flow if available.
  • Consider prescription of oral corticosteroid burst if asthma exacerbation confirmed.
  • Provide prescription or recommend OTC non-sedating antihistamine pending assessment.
- Doctor to send summary letter via app for patient to present to GP.
- Education: Seek urgent care (emergency services) if breathing worsens, unable to speak in sentences, or develops chest tightness, dizziness, or lip/finger cyanosis.
- Follow-up: GP review expected to take ~10 minutes; further follow-up per GP findings.

Quality checks (document_quality):

● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Complete medication list (names, doses, frequencies).
  - Drug allergies beyond patient’s recollection.
  - Smoking and alcohol history.
  - Vital signs and objective respiratory examination.
  - Immunization and other preventive screening history.

● Internal conflicts: None noted.

● Transcript quality: Generally clear but some dropped audio/ incomplete words; no quantitative clinical data provided.
